newsitem.title: FRANCE: Flexible approach needed to save EMU - Giscard.
newsitem.headline: Flexible approach needed to save EMU - Giscard.

text.p: Europe must interpret Maastricht treaty criteria flexibly if it wants to start the single currency on time, former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said on Thursday.

"If Europe clings to the strict criteria, not a single major country will be able to meet them except by resorting to accounting tricks, and the European project will fail," Giscard d'Estaing wrote in an opinion column published in the International Herald Tribune.
He said Europe had to decide whether the advantages of starting a single currency on time outweighed the risks.

"If the answer is 'yes,' the euro's success will depend on a joint reinterpretation of the Maastricht treaty, replacing its strict budgetary criteria with a more flexible approach based on progress toward reducing deficits, with the condition that the stability pact's requirements be maintained," Giscard d'Estaing said.
He said the stability pact, aimed at ensuring budget discipline, was crucial for the new currency's credibility, especially in persuading the German public to replace the mark with the euro.
"From here on in, the euro's main obstacle is going to be German public resistance," Giscard d'Estaing said.
The former president said the timely launch of the euro single currency, planned for January 1999, was "an imperative".
"We need it to bring about a stable unified market, encourage competition on an even playing field and attract international investment," he said.
"We must save the euro, and make it succeed."
